key_insight: A multi-modal transformer that fuses raw nanopore signals, wavelet images, and hand-crafted features can identify peptides more accurately than single-representation methods.
engineering_relevance: This approach could improve portable nanopore diagnostics by making molecular classification more robust to noisy, complex blockade signals.
method: Jointly encodes three signal views: time-series, wavelet-based image, and static feature vector.
Uses transformer-based attention to integrate complementary information across modalities.
Analyzes attention to show different modalities focus on different aspects of the same event.
evidence_signal: The model improves performance by more than 10 percentage points on a 42-peptide benchmark and transfers to a 20-amino-acid dataset with near-perfect accuracy.
watch_item: Performance may depend on high-quality, well-aligned multi-modal inputs, so deployment could be sensitive to preprocessing and dataset shift.
paper_title: Multi-modal transformer for signal classification in nanopore blockade experiments
